newsitem.title: TANZANIA: African leaders keep sanctions on Burundi.
newsitem.headline: African leaders keep sanctions on Burundi.

text.p: African leaders agreed on Saturday to maintain their economic embargo against war-torn Burundi despite a suggestion from the United States that sanctions should be eased.
"The summit reiterated that the objective of the sanctions is to serve as an effective means of securing a negotiated settlement between all parties to the conflict," they said in a statement.

The leaders said they had received a letter from Burundi's Tutsi military ruler Pierre Buyoya commiting himself to unconditional negotiations with the Hutu National Council for the Defence of Democracy and other armed Hutu rebel groups.
But the leaders said they would send a ministerial delegation to Burundi to ascertain Buyoya's seriousness.
"Heads of state gave the warring parties in Burundi a period of one month from Saturday in which to start negotiations or face unspecified measures from the regional group," the leaders said.
"The summit agreed to take measures against any group in Burundi that refuses to take part in the peace process," their statement said in the Tanzanian town of Arusha without giving details.
U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher on Friday suggested to East African leaders in Arusha that they should ease sanctions because of some progress towards national reconciliation.
